questions.q: Why does connection pooling matter more operationally for PostgreSQL than for a thread-based engine like SQL Server, per this lesson?
options: PostgreSQL forks a full OS process per connection, which has real memory/CPU cost and a lower practical connection ceiling
PostgreSQL doesn't support more than 10 connections at all without pooling
PgBouncer is required for PostgreSQL to accept any client connections whatsoever
SQL Server has no concept of connections
questions.explain: PostgreSQL's process-per-connection architecture (from Chapter 12) makes unpooled high-connection-count workloads expensive in a way thread-based engines aren't.

options: It sits between client applications and PostgreSQL, maintaining a small pool of real backend connections reused across many clients
It converts PostgreSQL's process-per-connection model into a thread-per-connection model
It is a PostgreSQL extension that runs inside the database server process itself
It replaces PostgreSQL's WAL-based replication mechanism
questions.explain: PgBouncer is a separate lightweight pooler that clients connect to, which hands out a smaller set of real PostgreSQL backend connections.

questions.q: Which PgBouncer pooling mode holds a server connection only for the duration of a single transaction?
options: Statement pooling
Connection pooling
Transaction pooling
Session pooling
questions.explain: Transaction pooling assigns a server connection per transaction and returns it to the pool immediately after, which is why it's the mode most deployments run.

questions.q: What is the main tradeoff of transaction pooling, per this lesson?
options: Session state like SET statements can't be relied on to persist across transactions, since the next transaction may land on a different backend
It provides worse connection reuse than session pooling
It cannot be used with any web application
It requires disabling replication entirely
questions.explain: Because the server connection is returned to the pool after each transaction, session-scoped state isn't guaranteed to survive to the next transaction.

questions.q: Which pooling mode is described as maximizing reuse but being the most restrictive, since it breaks multi-statement transactions?
options: Session pooling
Transaction pooling
Hot standby pooling
Statement pooling
questions.explain: Statement pooling releases the connection after every individual statement, which is incompatible with most real multi-statement application transactions.
